author: NTD
title: Dyson Launches $500 AI Toothbrush With Camera and Mouthrinse Jet
text:
Dyson is now selling a $499.99 electric toothbrush with a camera and an automated mouthrinse jet.
websitelists the product as out of stock.
press release.
The CameraJet uses a small camera near the brush head to look for spaces between teeth. Software analyzes 28 live images per second and activates a targeted mouthrinse spray when it detects a gap, according to Dyson. The device is intended to combine brushing, interdental cleaning, and rinsing into a single routine.
“Flossing is an awkward and time-consuming chore. Few of us do it even though we know we should. Dyson engineers and scientists have spent well over a decade understanding oral care regimes and how nasties build up in the mouth. Our research has shown that people consistently miss the areas where plaque forms: the gaps between teeth,” the company stated.
Dyson says it developed the system over six years with 661 engineers and input from 30 dental professionals. The company collected more than 470,000 dental images to develop the machine-learning system and filed 38 patent applications related to the device.
“We wanted to solve three fundamental problems: how to see those gaps, remove plaque, and how to improve cleaning performance while brushing,” Dyson said.
The Dyson CameraJet is Wi-Fi-connected at 2.4 GHz and Bluetooth-connected. Its integrated camera is a high-quality endoscope, allowing users to see what their dentist sees through the live-viewing feature in the MyDyson app, the company says.
“The camera is only active during live viewing or auto-jetting. No images are recorded or stored on the product or in the cloud, and images remain private to the user,” the company stated.
The company claims the toothbrush removed up to 69 percent more plaque in hard-to-reach areas than market-leading premium electric toothbrushes during laboratory testing. Dyson also cites a six-week study of 204 participants to support claims about improved gum health compared with a manual toothbrush.
The toothbrush contains a 12.5-milliliter mouthrinse tank and comes with a charging and refill dock, two brush heads, and a charging cable.
Dyson said that it is also introducing its own low-foaming mouthrinse and nonfoaming toothpaste, designed to prevent foam from blocking the camera.
